units.name: My School and My Community
units.summary: The people who help in a community, and the work they do.

topics.name: People Who Help Us
topics.summary: The jobs people do that keep a community working.

objectives.text: Name some jobs people do that help a community.
Say what would happen if one of those jobs was not done.
Say how people in a community depend on each other.

keyTerms.definition: All the people who live near each other in one place.
The work a person does, often to earn money or to help others.
To need someone else for something you cannot do yourself.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
Many people do work that helps everyone.

You will learn about some of those jobs.

You will learn why they matter.

sections.heading: Jobs that help everyone
sections.body:
Think about the people around where you live.

    A TEACHER helps children learn to read and count.

    A NURSE helps people who are sick or hurt.

    A FARMER grows the food that people eat.

    A SHOPKEEPER sells things people need.

    A DRIVER takes people and goods from place to place.

    A BUILDER makes the houses people live in.

None of these people works only for themselves. Their work reaches other people too.

sections.heading: What if the job was not done?
sections.body:
This is the best way to see why a job matters. Take it away and look.

If no farmer grew food, the shopkeeper would have nothing to sell, and nobody would eat.

If no driver carried goods, the food would stay on the farm and rot.

If no teacher taught, children would not learn to read.

If no nurse worked, a sick person would have nowhere to go.

Every job is holding something up. You notice it most when it stops.
sections.example:
One loaf of bread.

Think about bread on a table.

A farmer grew the grain.

A driver carried it to town.

A baker turned it into bread.

A shopkeeper sold it.

Someone in the family carried it home.

Five people. One loaf of bread.

Not one of them could have done it alone. The farmer cannot bake. The baker cannot grow grain. They each did one part, and together the bread reached the table.

sections.heading: Depending on each other
sections.body:
Nobody can do everything.

The nurse cannot also grow all her own food.

The farmer cannot also treat his own illness.

So the nurse depends on the farmer for food. The farmer depends on the nurse when he is sick.

That is what a community is: people who each do one thing well, and depend on each other for the rest.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
Think about where you live. Answer out loud.

1. Name three people who do work that helps others.

2. What does a nurse do?

3. What would happen if nobody grew food?

4. Who helps you learn?

5. Name one job you would like to do when you are older. Who would it help?

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• Many people do work that helps the whole community.
• Take a job away and you see what it was holding up.
• Nobody can do everything alone.
• People in a community depend on each other.

questions.question: Whose work grows the food that people eat?
questions.explanation: A farmer grows the food. The driver may carry it and the shopkeeper may sell it, but it starts with the farmer growing it.

questions.question: What does it mean to say people in a community depend on each other?
options: Everyone does exactly the same job
Each person does one thing well and needs others for the rest
Only some people are allowed to work
questions.explanation: Nobody can do everything. A nurse cannot also grow all her own food, and a farmer cannot treat his own illness. Each does one thing well and relies on others for the rest. That is what a community is.
